# Motley Play

> Books and puzzles for the curious mind. A collection of books, puzzles, and games that inspire creativity and curiosity.

Last updated: 2026-10-13

## Advanced Kakuro Tactics

- [The Ultimate Guide to Advanced Kakuro Tactics](https://motleyplay.com/posts/advanced-kakuro-tactics-guide/): Advanced Kakuro tactics in one place: magic blocks, intersections, the 45 rule, and parity. Solve expert grids without guessing, with a worked example.
- [Essential Magic Blocks: The Kakuro Cheat Sheet](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-magic-blocks/): Memorize the 16 Kakuro magic blocks for 2 to 5 cells, then use them to find every entry point on an expert grid. Includes a cheat sheet and a worked example.
- [Mastering the 45 Rule in Kakuro](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-45-rule/): Kakuro has no 3x3 boxes, so the Sudoku 45 rule needs a twist. Learn the long-entry trick and how innies and outies crack open blocks with no magic blocks.
- [Intersection Logic: Cross-Referencing Kakuro Clues](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-intersection-logic/): Learn to read Kakuro clues in pairs: how high and low sums crossing each other force single digits, plus a cheat sheet of the crossings that solve corners.
- [Eliminating Guesswork in Kakuro: Parity and Logic](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-eliminating-guesswork/): Stop guessing on expert Kakuro puzzles. Use parity rules, ghost duplicates, and short forcing chains to settle stuck corners with logic, not a coin flip.

## Kakuro for Beginners

- [The Complete Beginner's Guide to Solving Kakuro](https://motleyplay.com/posts/beginner-kakuro-guide/): New to Kakuro? Learn to read the grid, spot the unique sums that start every solve, and cross-reference clues to place every digit without a single guess.
- [Understanding Kakuro Rules and Grid Mechanics](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-rules-grid-mechanics/): Learn the Kakuro rules that trip up new solvers: which way each clue points, where an entry starts and stops, and why one row can legally hold two 5s.
- [Kakuro Unique Sums: The Magic of 3, 4, 16, and 17](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-unique-sums/): Every Kakuro solve starts with unique sums. Learn why 3, 4, 16, and 17 in two cells have only one answer, then use them to crack a full practice grid.
- [How to Cross-Reference Intersecting Kakuro Clues](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-cross-referencing-clues/): Know the digits but not their order? Learn how to cross-reference Kakuro clues where across and down entries meet to find forced digits, step by step.
- [Common Kakuro Mistakes Beginners Make and How to Avoid Them](https://motleyplay.com/posts/common-kakuro-mistakes/): Guessing, hidden duplicates, stale pencil marks, and addition slips ruin most beginner Kakuro grids. Here's how to catch each habit and stop it early.
- [Transitioning from Sudoku to Kakuro: What Changes?](https://motleyplay.com/posts/sudoku-to-kakuro/): Good at Sudoku but stuck on Kakuro? See which habits carry over, why the no-repeat rule works differently, and how your favorite Sudoku tricks map to Kakuro.

## Kakuro Puzzle Design

- [How to Make a Kakuro Puzzle From Scratch](https://motleyplay.com/posts/how-to-make-kakuro/): Build a Kakuro from blank paper: lay out the grid, fill the digits, find and fix a second solution, then set the difficulty, all on one worked 7x7 grid.
- [Designing a Kakuro Grid: Symmetry, Runs and Black Cells](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-grid-design/): Kakuro grid layout rules: runs of 2 to 9 cells, every white cell crossed both ways, 180-degree symmetry, and how black cells shape a solve. A worked 7x7.
- [How to Make Sure Your Kakuro Has Exactly One Solution](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-unique-solution/): Why your Kakuro has two solutions, why a magic block won't fix a digit swap, and how one changed digit and two new clues make the series 7x7 grid unique.
- [How to Set Kakuro Difficulty: Technique, Not Grid Size](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-difficulty-levels/): Kakuro difficulty comes from the hardest technique a grid needs, not its size. Grade a 7x7 as Medium, then refill the same layout so it needs a region count.
- [Build a Kakuro Solver and Generator in Python](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-solver-generator/): Write a Kakuro solver in Python with combination tables and backtracking, then turn it into a generator that checks for a second solution and grades difficulty.
- [Designing Kakuro Grids That Hide an Answer](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-hidden-answers/): Build a Kakuro grid around a hidden code: pick the answer cells, dodge the digit traps, lock them in, fill around them, and make sure the answer arrives late.

## Playable Puzzles

Free murder-mystery puzzles you can play in your browser: a logic grid, a Victorian cryptogram, a detective-themed connections board, and a mansion escape.

- [Death at Ravenscroft Manor: A Murder Mystery Logic Grid](https://motleyplay.com/games/mansion-murder-logic/): Four guests, four rooms, one dead lord. Solve a free murder-mystery logic grid in your browser using nine clues and pure deduction. No guessing.
- [The Detective's Maxim: A Victorian Cryptogram](https://motleyplay.com/games/victorian-cryptogram/): Crack a substitution cipher hiding a famous line from Sherlock Holmes. Type one letter and every match updates. Free to play in your browser.
- [Detective Clues: A Murder Mystery Connections Puzzle](https://motleyplay.com/games/detective-clues-connections/): Sixteen words, four hidden groups, four mistakes allowed. A detective-themed connections puzzle with a red herring or two. Free to play in your browser.
- [The Blackwood Estate: A Victorian Murder Escape](https://motleyplay.com/games/blackwood-estate-escape/): Locked in a Yorkshire manor with a body in the study. Crack two locks, test three alibis and name the killer in a free text-based escape game.
